assumedContext: No primary filing could be retrieved: every external domain is blocked by this environment egress proxy. Findings rest on search-result summaries.

findings.claim: FY2025 revenue was USD 402.836bn, up 15%, with net income of USD 132.170bn and diluted EPS of USD 10.81.
findings.label: FACT

findings.claim: Q1 2026 revenue was USD 109.9bn — an eleventh consecutive quarter of double-digit growth — with operating income up 30% to USD 39.7bn and operating margin of 36.1%.
findings.label: FACT

findings.claim: Q2 2026 revenue was USD 119.8bn, up 24%, with operating income up 30% to USD 40.8bn. Growth is accelerating, not decaying.
findings.label: FACT

findings.claim: Google Cloud revenue reached USD 24.8bn in Q2 2026, up 82%, with operating income of USD 8.8bn — more than tripling year on year — and operating margin of 35.6% against 20.7% a year earlier.
findings.label: FACT

findings.claim: Cloud backlog stood at USD 514bn at Q2 2026 — more than four times FY2025 total company revenue and roughly nine times annualised Cloud revenue.
findings.label: FACT

findings.claim: Search revenue grew 17% to USD 63.3bn in Q2 2026, and YouTube advertising reached USD 11.06bn against USD 9.79bn a year earlier. The core advertising franchise is accelerating despite two years of predictions that generative AI would erode it.
findings.label: FACT

findings.claim: FY2026 consensus revenue is approximately USD 488-498bn for growth of about 21%, with FY2027 consensus of approximately USD 585.6bn for growth of about 20%.
findings.label: CONSENSUS
findings.source: Analyst consensus via Simply Wall St and Fundamentalis, 2026

findings.claim: Demand classification: Cloud backlog of USD 514bn is [Existing Contracted]; the Search and YouTube advertising base is [Existing Contracted] in substance; multi-gigawatt TPU supply agreements are [Approved / Committed Pipeline]; the 20-city Waymo expansion is [Unfunded Planned Project]; and a re-rating from AI leadership is [Speculative Demand] and earns zero base-case weight.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE

findings.claim: Growth is margin-accretive at the group level: operating income grew 30% in both Q1 and Q2 2026 against revenue growth of 16% and 24% respectively, and consolidated operating margin expanded two points to 36.1% in Q1.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.source: Derived from reported Q1 and Q2 2026 figures

findings.claim: Incremental margin in Cloud is far above the segment average — operating income more than tripled on 82% revenue growth — so the fastest-growing segment is also the one improving group margin. This is the opposite of the growth-dilutes-returns trap.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE

findings.claim: Other Bets remains immaterial to revenue and a persistent drag on profit: USD 382m of revenue against a USD 1.8bn operating loss in Q2 2026, and USD 411m against USD 2.1bn in Q1.
findings.label: FACT

gaps.whyItMatters: Aggregate Search growth of 17% could mask falling monetisation offset by rising volume, which would matter for the terminal case.
Unquantified and potentially material to the return on the capex programme.

risks.text: Cloud growth of 82% is not sustainable indefinitely; the market is capitalising a rate that must decay.
Search growth could be volume-driven with falling monetisation per query, which aggregate disclosure would hide.
Other Bets loses roughly USD 7-8bn a year with immaterial revenue and no disclosed path to profit.

catalysts.text: Q3 2026 results — whether Cloud growth holds above 60% and Search above 15%
Backlog conversion disclosure in the FY2026 10-K

conclusions: This is a business accelerating at USD 400bn+ of scale: revenue growth from 15% in FY2025 to a consensus 21% in FY2026, with operating income growing 30% in both reported quarters.

Cloud is the engine and it is compounding profitably — 82% growth with operating margin expanding from 20.7% to 35.6%, behind USD 514bn of contracted backlog worth more than four times total company revenue.
The AI-kills-Search thesis is not visible in the numbers. Search grew 17% year on year in Q2 2026, two years after the disruption was first predicted.
Growth is accretive at every level examined. The fastest-growing segment carries the highest incremental margin, which is the opposite of the trap this protocol exists to catch.
Applying the classification discipline flatters Alphabet unusually: most of the demand sits in [Existing Contracted], not in narrative. Only the re-rating case is speculative.
thesisImpact: Phase 3 makes the operating case unusually strong and narrows the bear argument to two things: the durability of Cloud growth rates, and whether reported profit survives an honest depreciation assumption on the assets generating it. Nothing in the demand picture supports a bear case; the risk is entirely in cost recognition and capital intensity.
